requests.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Six OPEN LINE DRAWINGS of fixed cosmic regions for an illustrated combination game, in a precise 3-column 2-row atlas. Landscape 3:2. Each complete drawing has its own equal square cell with generous transparent margin, maximum 78 percent cell width. REAL transparent background including ALL openings. No circles, medallions, frames, opaque cell backgrounds, labels, arrows or text. These are freely drawn sparse physical surroundings, clearly different from the filled circular inventory illustrations in the reference.
Use the reference's palette and mark character but DARK charcoal/slate LINE ART only with minimal small amber accents. Strong simple contours readable at128px; hatching sparse, all negative space transparent. Do not paint broad shaded masses. Lineweight approximately 6 sourcepixels for a400pixel drawing. Each subject roughly width1.4:height1.
Exact row-major subjects:
1. Sparse stellar outskirts: two broad broken curved arcs carrying 12 widely separated small star stipples; plenty of open space and no bright central star, no arrows.
2. Crowded dark lane: fork-shaped irregular gas contours with three dense outlined pockets on its branches. Sparse broad hatching only within pockets. No newborn stars.
3. Young disk: one modest warm cream central star, broad open elliptical dusty-disk contours, near-side notch, no planets or moons. The same disk shape as reference, but open line drawing.
4. Existing massive black-hole surroundings BEFORE feeding: a SMALL completely dark oval gap bounded by broken sparse gas contour arcs. No bright rim, no large torus, no jet, no glowing material. Most of drawing remains transparent. Dark region is only one-fifth drawingwidth.
5. Polar surroundings outside a nuclear disk: six gently tapering curved field-guide strokes, separate and open with broad gaps, a few tiny gas flecks, no arrows, no bright jet or star, no dark hole. The strokes indicate physical region outside the centre.
6. Compact triangular star cluster: a compact triangular group of discrete modest star points plus one smaller offset knot of three warm dots, sparse broken gascontours around it. Not a connected triangle or constellation diagram.
Ensure each subject entirely within own cell. Preserve broad grouping and physically meaningful shapes, no literal planetforming rings in emptyreceivers.
